# Load data

```{r}
rm(list=ls())

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(reghelper)

#setwd("mypath")

# main dataset from experimental sessions including: momentary psychological measures, salivary cortisol (sCort) and salivary alpha amylase (sAA); all measures  have one value per study measurement point (once an hour or once every two hours)
dat <- read_excel("lab_data_main_2022-03-08.xlsx")

# heart rate (HR) dataset from experimental sessions; one value per minute
dat_hr <- read_excel("lab_data_HR_2022-03-08.xlsx")

# dataset of psychological measures, sCort, and sAA collected the morning after each session; one value per morning
dat_m  <- read_excel("lab_data_morning_2022-05-06.xlsx")

```

# Outline variables

```{r}
# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Grouping and independent variables ---

# subject number of each participant
dat$ID <- as.factor(dat$ID)
dat_hr$ID <- as.factor(dat_hr$ID)
dat_m$ID <- as.factor(dat_m$ID)


# experimental condition - "Baseline" is a reference category compared to "Fasting" and "Isolation"
dat$Condition <- as.factor(dat$Condition)
dat$Condition <- factor(dat$Condition, levels = c("Baseline", "Isolation", "Fasting"))

dat_hr$Condition <- as.factor(dat_hr$Condition)
dat_hr$Condition <- factor(dat_hr$Condition, levels = c("Baseline", "Isolation", "Fasting"))

dat_m$Condition <- as.factor(dat_m$Condition)
dat_m$Condition <- factor(dat_m$Condition, levels = c("Baseline", "Isolation", "Fasting"))

# time since first momentary measurement (right upon the start of the session) point in hours; 0 = 11am, 8 = 7pm
dat$hours_num <- as.numeric(dat$hours_num)
# hour count since the start of the session; 1 = aggregate of the bpm measures from 11:00 to 12:00, 8 = aggregate of the bpm measures from 18:00 to 19:00
dat_hr$hours <- as.numeric(dat_hr$hours)

# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Dependent variables: psychological momentary measures ---

# Loneliness: "How lonely do you feel at the moment?", VAS 0-100 
dat$loneliness_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$loneliness_VAS)

# Desire for social contact: "How strong is your desire for social contact right now?", VAS 0-100
dat$desire_soc_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$desire_soc_VAS)

# Hunger: "How hungry do you feel at the moment?", VAS 0-100
dat$hunger_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$hunger_VAS)

# Desire for food: "How strong is your desire for food at the moment?", VAS 0-100
dat$desire_food_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$desire_food_VAS)

# Stress: "How stressed do you feel?", VAS 0-100
dat$stress_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$stress_VAS)

# Anxiety: "How anxious you feel at the moment?", VAS 0-100
dat$anxiety_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$anxiety_VAS)

# Controllability: "How much do you have the situation under control?", VAS 0-100
dat$control_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$control_VAS)

# Avoidance: "How strong is your need to leave this situation?", VAS 0-100
dat$avoid_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$avoid_VAS)

# Multidimensional mood questionnaire (MDBF) (see Steyer et al., 2003)
# Short form A and Short form B were alternated every measurement point (every odd participant number started with the form A and every even participant with the form B); a score for each measurement point is formed by addition of 4 items per scale 
# "At the moment, I feel..." (1 = "not at all", 5 = "very")

# MDBF, mood valence
dat$MDBF_valence_mood <- as.numeric(dat$MDBF_valence_mood)

# MDBF, calmness
dat$MDBF_calmness_mood <- as.numeric(dat$MDBF_calmness_mood)

# MDBF, energetic arousal 
dat$MDBF_energy_mood <- as.numeric(dat$MDBF_energy_mood)

# Multidimensional fatigue inventory (MFI, adaptation) (see Doerr et al., 2017 and Doerr et al., 2021, adapted from Lin et al, 2009)
# "At the moment, I feel..." (1 = "not at all", 5 = "very")

# MFI, general fatigue
dat$MFI_general_fatigue <- as.numeric(dat$MFI_general_fatigue)

# MFI, physical fatigue
dat$MFI_physical_fatigue <- as.numeric(dat$MFI_physical_fatigue)

# MFI, mental fatigue
dat$MFI_mental_fatigue <- as.numeric(dat$MFI_mental_fatigue)

# MFI, reduced motivation
dat$MFI_reduced_motivation <- as.numeric(dat$MFI_reduced_motivation)

# MFI, reduced activity
dat$MFI_reduced_activity <- as.numeric(dat$MFI_reduced_activity)

# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Dependent variables: physiological measures ---

# sCort (nmol/L) - collected once an hour, logarithmically transformed (ln(x) + 10)
dat$sCortt <- log10(dat$sCort)

# area under curve with respect to ground (AUCg) for sCort (Pruessner et al., 2003) - logarithmically transformed (ln(x) + 10)
dat$AUCg_sCort_t <- log10(dat$AUCg_sCort)

# area under curve with respect to increase (AUCi) for sCort (Pruessner et al., 2003)
dat$AUCi_sCort <- as.numeric(dat$AUCi_sCort)

# sAA (U/mL) - collected once an hour, logarithmically transformed (ln(x) + 10)
dat$sAAt <- log10(dat$sAA)

# area under curve with respect to ground (AUCg) for sAA (Pruessner et al., 2003) - logarithmically transformed (ln(x) + 10)
dat$AUCg_sAA_t <- log10(dat$AUCg_sAA)

# area under curve with respect to increase (AUCi) for sAA (Pruessner et al., 2003)
dat$AUCi_sAA <- as.numeric(dat$AUCi_sAA)

# HR - beats per minute (bpm) collected throughout the session
dat_hr$M_bpm <- as.numeric(dat_hr$M_bpm)

# area under curve with respect to ground (AUCg) for HR
dat_hr$AUCg_Mbpm <- as.numeric(dat_hr$AUCg_Mbpm)

# area under curve with respect to increase (AUCi) for HR
dat_hr$AUCi_Mbpm <- as.numeric(dat_hr$AUCi_Mbpm)


# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Dependent variables: next morning psychological measures ---

# Loneliness: "How lonely do you feel at the moment?", VAS 0-100 
dat_m$loneliness_VAS <- as.numeric(dat_m$loneliness_VAS)

# Desire for social contact: "How strong is your desire for social contact right now?", VAS 0-100
dat_m$desire_soc_VAS <- as.numeric(dat_m$desire_soc_VAS)

# Hunger: "How hungry do you feel at the moment?", VAS 0-100
dat_m$hunger_VAS <- as.numeric(dat_m$hunger_VAS)

# Desire for food: "How strong is your desire for food at the moment?", VAS 0-100
dat_m$desire_food_VAS <- as.numeric(dat_m$desire_food_VAS)

# Stress: "How stressed do you feel?", VAS 0-100
dat_m$stress_VAS <- as.numeric(dat_m$stress_VAS)

# Anxiety: "How anxious you feel at the moment?", VAS 0-100
dat_m$anxiety_VAS <- as.numeric(dat_m$anxiety_VAS)

# Controllability: "How much do you have the situation under control?", VAS 0-100
dat_m$control_VAS <- as.numeric(dat_m$control_VAS)

# Avoidance: "How strong is your need to leave this situation?", VAS 0-100
dat_m$avoid_VAS <- as.numeric(dat_m$avoid_VAS)

# Multidimensional mood questionnaire (MDBF) (see Steyer et al., 2003), mood valence 
dat_m$MDBF_valence_mood <- as.numeric(dat_m$MDBF_valence_mood)

# MDBF, calmness
dat_m$MDBF_calmness_mood <- as.numeric(dat_m$MDBF_calmness_mood)

# MDBF, energetic arousal 
dat_m$MDBF_energy_mood <- as.numeric(dat_m$MDBF_energy_mood)

# Multidimensional fatigue inventory (MFI, adaptation) (see Doerr et al., 2017 and Doerr et al., 2021, adapted from Lin et al, 2009), general fatigue
dat_m$MFI_general_fatigue <- as.numeric(dat_m$MFI_general_fatigue)

# MFI, physical fatigue
dat_m$MFI_physical_fatigue <- as.numeric(dat_m$MFI_physical_fatigue)

# MFI, mental fatigue
dat_m$MFI_mental_fatigue <- as.numeric(dat_m$MFI_mental_fatigue)

# MFI, reduced motivation
dat_m$MFI_reduced_motivation <- as.numeric(dat_m$MFI_reduced_motivation)

# MFI, reduced activity
dat_m$MFI_reduced_activity <- as.numeric(dat_m$MFI_reduced_activity)


# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Dependent variables: next morning physiological measures ---

# Cortisol awakening response (CAR), awakening value substracted from value collected 30min after awakening
dat_m$CAR <- as.numeric(dat_m$CAR)

# S1 for sCort - morning sCort value collected upon awakening - logarithmically transformed (ln(x) + 10)
dat_m$sCort_S1_t <- log10(dat_m$sCort_S1)

# Alpha amylase awakening response (CAR), awakening value substracted from value collected 30min after awakening
dat_m$AAR <- as.numeric(dat_m$AAR)

# S1 for sAA - morning sAA value collected upon awakening - logarithmically transformed (ln(x) + 10)
dat_m$sCAA_S1_t <- log10(dat_m$sAA_S1)


# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Variables used for dropout exclusion ---

# Criterion for participant exclusion for sCort and sAA (see SM6). Outlier values were identified from the first measurements (before the start) of each session, which would indicate that participants already started a condition with higher sCort or sAA values. The threshold for exclusion was more than three standard deviations higher or lower than the average baseline value for a given condition (Stalder et al., 2016). Participants with outlier baseline values for at least one condition were excluded.

paste("number of participants excluded from sAA analysis:", length(unique(dat$ID[dat$sAAt_dropout])))
paste("number of participants excluded from sCort analysis:", length(unique(dat$ID[dat$sCortt_dropout])))

# Criterion for participant exclusion for HR: loss of data in the baseline condition (for two participants entire baseline condition and for one participants last 6 hours)
paste("number of participants excluded from HR analysis:", length(unique(dat_hr$ID[dat_hr$HR_drop])))

```

# Preparation of data sets for the aggregate measures

```{r}

dat_ag <-
  dat %>%
    group_by(ID, Condition) %>%
    summarise(AUCg_sCort_t = mean(AUCg_sCort_t),
              AUCi_sCort = mean(AUCi_sCort),
              AUCg_sAA_t = mean(AUCg_sAA_t),
              AUCi_sAA = mean(AUCi_sAA))

dat_hr_ag <-
  dat_hr %>%
    group_by(ID, Condition) %>%
    summarise(AUCg_Mbpm = mean(AUCg_Mbpm),
              AUCi_Mbpm = mean(AUCi_Mbpm))

  
```

# Run models

# Psychological momentary measures

## 1. Loneliness

### Main effect of condition

```{r}

mod.loneliness_me <- lmer(loneliness_VAS ~ Condition + hours_num + (Condition|ID), data = dat, REML = TRUE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

# Random effect structure of more complex models that did not converge:
#   (Condition+hours_num|ID) boundary (singular) fit: see ?isSingular 

summary(mod.loneliness_me)

```


### Interaction between condition and time

```{r}

mod.loneliness_int <- lmer(loneliness_VAS ~ Condition*hours_num + (Condition|ID), data = dat, REML = TRUE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

# Random effect structure of more complex models that did not converge:
#   (Condition*hours_num|ID) boundary (singular) fit: see ?isSingular Model failed to converge with 1 negative eigenvalue: -3.9e-03
#   (Condition+hours_num|ID) boundary (singular) fit: see ?isSingular

summary(mod.loneliness_int)

# simple slope analysis of interaction between baseline:isolation and time
simple_slopes(mod.loneliness_int, levels=list(Condition=c("Baseline", "Isolation")))

```

# Physiological measures

## 1. sCort - momentary values

### Main effect of condition

```{r}

mod.cort_me <- lmer(sCortt ~ Condition + hours_num + (Condition + hours_num|ID), data = dat[-which(dat$sCortt_dropout==TRUE),], REML = TRUE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))
# To check results without outlier removal (reported in Supplementary Table 5), change data assignment to "data = dat".

summary(mod.cort_me)

# adjusted p values - Bonferroni correction
p1<- summary(mod.cort_me)$coefficients[,"Pr(>|t|)"]
p_adjusted <- p1*3
round(p_adjusted,3)[2:4]



```

### Interaction between condition and time

```{r}

mod.cort_int <- lmer(sCortt ~ Condition * hours_num + (Condition + hours_num|ID), data = dat[-which(dat$sCortt_dropout==TRUE),], REML = TRUE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))
# To check results without outlier removal (reported in Supplementary Table 5), change data assignment to "data = dat".

# Random effect structure of more complex models that did not converge:
#   (Condition * hours_num|ID) boundary (singular) fit: see ?isSingular

summary(mod.cort_int)

# adjusted p values - Bonferroni correction
p1<- summary(mod.cort_int)$coefficients[,"Pr(>|t|)"]
p_adjusted <- p1*3
round(p_adjusted,3)[5:6]

```
